raw_comment: Thanks to all the students who responded. Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  two headlines from Eaglecrest High School in Aurora, Colo. – “Dying of Thirst (and a Better Environment)” by Autumn and "Parched Nation: America's Drought Struggle Intensifies" by Analay, Avery and Connor;  “Rising Drought Threats: U.S. Faces Widespread Water Scarcity in Late 2024” by Massimo of Fla.; "The United States of Dehydration; Who’s Being Affected the Most?" by Wen of Andover High School in Mass.; two headlines from Gull Lake High School in Richland, Mich. –“Don’t Doubt the Drought, Dryness Starts to Scorch the U.S.” by Peyton and "Heartland in a Heat Grip: Drought Tightens on the Central States of the U.S." by Blake; “Climate Change Continues to Punish: U.S. Droughts Scatter and Persist” by Dialeski of Perth Amboy High School in N.J.; "Drought Aims at Red States Despite Denials of Global Warming" by Nestles of Berlin, N.H.; “Droughts: How the US is Feeling the Heat” by Rachael of Valley Stream North High School in N.Y.; “Extreme Drought Crisis in the United States: What Does This Mean for the Country?” by Katie of Academy of Saint Elizabeth in Convent Station, N.J.; “If in Doubt, Remember That We Are in a Drought” by Alex of Penn.; "Droughtful Times” by Alvin of Doylestown, Penn. and “A Nation in Thirst: American's Drought Struggle Intensifies” by Ms. Lasky’s AP Language class at Middleton High School in Wis.
